text: {"score":3,"justification":"The headline numbers match the card (12.8%, 4.0%, 6.79, z 1.23, 45 docs, 16 docs of 99215, 0 below, 5 of 29). The cautious, inconclusive stance is appropriate. But several narrative claims are unsupported by the card or contradict it, and the next steps are weak. An investigator would have to redo some of the checking.","problems":["Claims 'roughly a third of returned notes show a duplicate-text signal' and 'some repeated times'; the card has no duplicate-text or repeated-time data (note-check figures of problems/late/unsigned/data appear only in the summary, and none show a 33% duplicate rate). This looks unsupported or fabricated.","Says 'elevated 99215 rate holds in every complexity tier, roughly double the all-provider share even among zero- and one-condition patients'; the 0-condition tier is 0.066 vs 0.022 (3x) and 1-condition 0.081 vs 0.035 (2.3x), so 'roughly double' is imprecise, though the direction is right.","Cited examples C0009183 and C0010234 are described as 'follow-up visits' based on Z09 codes, which is an interpretation; and the summary's own list says 99215 for R21/Z09 etc. The 99215 with the 'routine' label is a stretch but plausible.","Cites C0010179 (a 99214 documented as low MDM) as an example although the focus is 99215; it is the only below-billed case but is not a 99215 claim and reads as a mismatched exemplar.","Next steps are generic and partly circular: request charts 'starting with' C0010179, which already has documentation, and offers no concrete step like a larger random sample or comparison with high-complexity 99215s; the audit trail request is only in the rationale.","Compares 0% to 14% comparison providers, which matches the card's 0.143. But the summary does not note that the sample of 16 is too small to compare. The 'weak support' caveat is partly given."]}
